identity.name: Kaleb Dida Abera
identity.title: Aspiring cognitive scientist. Human-centered AI and software.
identity.tagline: Minds, machines, and the locks between them.
identity.intro: I'm Kal, an aspiring cognitive scientist from Adama. I build human-centered software, play CTFs, and want to become an AI engineer.

about.lead: I care about three things that turn out to be one thing: how minds work, how to build machines that think, and how to keep those machines safe.
paragraphs: I graduated from Adama Science and Technology University Special School (ASTU SPS) in July 2026, first in my section every year. This is my gap year before studying cognitive science: I’m building Logbook, competing in CTFs, and teaching weekly Bible lessons to kids in my neighborhood.

Logbook is what I’m building right now. It’s a private, offline-first journal with an AI companion that asks me a question every day and remembers past entries and photos. It’s how I’ve been exploring whether software can support memory and self-reflection.
Before that came a summer of neuroscience research with ThinkNeuro, the INSA cyber talent program, a four-person robotics team I led, and a Peace Club I founded that grew to 63 members.

disciplines.title: AI and cognitive science
disciplines.text: How minds remember, and how software can help. Logbook’s companion is my experiment in autobiographical memory. ThinkNeuro was my first research.

disciplines.title: Cybersecurity
disciplines.text: Selected for the INSA cyber talent program in grade 10. Three CTF contests so far, best finish 9th of 53 teams.

disciplines.title: Robotics
disciplines.text: In 2023 I led a team of four building a robot that senses and steers around obstacles. My first look at the perception-action loop.

offScreen.label: Keyboard and guitar
offScreen.text: I play both. Turn the sound on and the keys a to k on your keyboard play soft notes.

offScreen.label: Writing
offScreen.text: Lowercase journals on my Telegram channel. A piece on discipline in the digital age won an international prize.

offScreen.label: Teaching
offScreen.text: Sunday lessons for 12 kids in my neighborhood, and a summer school for 36 students.
